column1: # Fixed molecular clock rates for the Auspice time trees (augur refine --timetree --clock-rate; plan D8), used by
# PhyloAuspice. Substitutions per site per year; the clock std-dev passed to augur is rate / 5 (as Nextstrain does).
# Source of the segment-specific rates: nextstrain/seasonal-flu, workflow/snakemake_rules/core.smk L189-219 at commit
# MP and NS have no segment-specific rate there: seasonal-flu falls back to its generic 0.001 for them, and so does
# FluTyper (generic = yes -> PhyloAuspice logs a WARNING "generic rate, not segment-specific").
# Whole-genome tree: no row; PhyloAuspice uses the length-weighted mean of the 8 segment rates of the subtype (weights
# = the segment lengths in the tree's segments.tsv) and logs the value.
# A subtype/segment without a row gets no time tree (divergence-only export + WARNING); no rate is ever guessed.
# Columns (tab-separated): subtype, segment, rate, generic (yes/no), source. Lines starting with '#' are comments.
# H5 (AVIAN). Source of the rates: nextstrain/avian-flu, segment-focused/config.yaml at commit
#  - Those rates are keyed by SUBTYPE and by a 2-year build window. They say nothing about
#    clade 2.3.4.4b, and no clade-specific published rate was found. A 6-month dataset is
#    inside a 2-year window, so the 2y values are the closest citable ones.
#  - The h5nx values are used here, not the h5n1 ones, because FluTyper's H5 subtype matches on
#    the H tag alone: one H5 tree holds H5N1, H5N2, H5N3 and H5N4 tips, which is exactly the
#    case nextstrain covers with h5nx. For a run whose tips are all H5N1, pass
# nextstrain gives every H5 rate one fixed std-dev (0.00211); PhyloAuspice derives rate / 5, as
# it does for every other subtype, so the std-dev used here is not nextstrain's.
